title: Add runbook links to incident-bot output based on incident_type
author: Devon Price
description:
Context: As part of the Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping rollout, we want incident-bot to provide “next click” runbooks immediately after classification. Today we auto-resolve owner from incident_type/subtype, but the bot output still forces on-call to hunt for the right runbook.

This PR wires runbook link suggestions into the incident summary payload consumed by incident-bot. It uses the control-plane owner mapping config (type/subtype -> owner + runbook_links) when available, with a small static fallback mapping for top-level types while teams backfill links.

What changed (high level):
- Adds optional runbook link fields to the incident summary payload returned by the incident service: runbook_links[] (URL) + runbook_titles[] (display) + runbook_link_source (owner_mapping|fallback|none).
- Resolves links from owner-mapping config keyed by (incident_type, incident_subtype). If subtype has no links, falls back to type-level links. If still missing, uses a small allowlisted fallback map for the most common categories (overload, auth, routing/fallback, control plane, telemetry blind spot, private connectivity).
- Enforces safety/consistency rules:
  - Allowlist URL hosts: confluence.redwoodinference.com and github.com/redwoodinference/redwood.
  - Max 3 links emitted, deterministic ordering.
  - If incident_type is unknown/unclassified, emits no links (source=none).
- Adds a lightweight counter metric (no labels) for link coverage: incident_runbook_links_emitted_total and incident_runbook_links_missing_total.

Why it’s safe:
- New fields are additive and optional; incident-bot can ignore them until it updates.
- URL allowlist prevents accidental leakage of arbitrary URLs through config.

Testing:
- Unit tests for resolution precedence (subtype > type > fallback > none).
- Unit tests for URL allowlist and max link count.
- Manual: created a test incident with incident_type=capacity_and_overload / subtype=fleet_capacity_shortage and verified the summary includes the Fleet runbook links.

Rollout:
- Behind a server-side feature flag: incident_payload_runbook_links (default ON in staging, OFF in prod).
- Plan: enable for 10% of incidents for 24h, then ramp to 100% if dashboards show no errors.

Example output (truncated): incident_type=routing_and_fallback / incident_subtype=fallback_misbehavior
- runbook_links: ["https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Router+Fallback+Misbehavior+Runbook", "https://github.com/redwoodinference/redwood/blob/main/runbooks/routing/fallback-debugging.md"]
- runbook_link_source: owner_mapping

Notes:
- This PR intentionally does not modify incident-bot UI; it only adds the server payload so the bot can show it. Bot UI will consume these fields in incident-bot PR #812.
commits: Add runbook link fields to incident summary payload schema
Resolve runbook links from owner-mapping config (subtype/type precedence)
Add URL allowlist + max link count enforcement
Add fallback mapping for common incident types
Wire feature flag and staging defaults
review_conversation:
Rafael Mendes: Can we cap this at a small number of links and make ordering deterministic? Also please avoid new high-cardinality labels in metrics.
Devon Price: Added max=3, stable sort by title then URL, and changed metrics to two counters with no labels.

Kira Thompson: The fallback mapping worries me—please ensure we don’t suggest the generic overload runbook for Fleet capacity shortage. Can we keep fallback only at type-level and prefer config when subtype is present?
Devon Price: Updated precedence to subtype config > type config > fallback (type only). Also changed fallback entry for capacity_and_overload to point to Fleet capacity runbook rather than generic overload.

Ethan Park: Owner mapping config already supports runbook_links; please use that field rather than inventing a parallel mapping in code.
Devon Price: Confirmed: resolver reads runbook_links from control-plane owner mapping; static fallback only covers cases where runbook_links is empty/missing.

Allison Grant: URL allowlist is good. Please add a log event when a link is dropped due to non-allowlisted host so we can detect misconfig.
Devon Price: Added structured warn log with incident_type/subtype redacted to type-only (to avoid cardinality).

Dylan Brooks: Please add a feature flag and ship dark in prod. Also update docs so bot team knows which fields to read.
Devon Price: Added incident_payload_runbook_links flag; default OFF prod, ON staging. Added docs/ops/incident-payload-fields.md section for runbook fields.
release_notes: Internal: incident summary payload now includes optional runbook link suggestions keyed by incident_type/subtype (behind feature flag incident_payload_runbook_links).
